title: Find Lucky Integer in an Array
statement: Return the largest integer whose frequency in the array equals the integer itself, or -1 if none exists.
explanation: Count frequencies and choose the largest value whose count equals its value.

title: Minimum Subsequence in Non-Increasing Order
approach: Take largest values until majority sum
statement: Return the shortest subsequence, sorted non-increasingly, whose sum is greater than the sum of the remaining elements.
explanation: Sort descending and keep adding the largest values until their sum exceeds the sum of all remaining values.

title: Kids With the Greatest Number of Candies
statement: For each child, return whether giving them extraCandies would make their candy count at least the current maximum.
explanation: Compare each value plus extraCandies with the maximum original count.

title: Destination City
approach: Find city never appearing as an origin
statement: Given directed city paths that form one non-cyclic route, return the destination city with no outgoing path.
explanation: Collect all origin cities and return the path destination that is not in the origin set.

title: Build an Array With Stack Operations
approach: Simulate reading values from 1 through n
statement: Return Push and Pop operations to build target from the stream 1..n, stopping when target is complete.
explanation: For each stream value up to the target’s last value, push it; pop values not present in target.

title: Number of Students Doing Homework at a Given Time
statement: Count students whose startTime <= queryTime <= endTime.
explanation: Count intervals containing queryTime, including both endpoints.

title: Make Two Arrays Equal by Reversing Subarrays
statement: Return true if two arrays can be made equal using reversals of any subarrays.
explanation: Reversals can produce any permutation, so the arrays must have identical value frequencies.

title: Shuffle the Array
explanation: Append corresponding elements from the first and second halves in alternating order.

title: Final Prices With a Special Discount in a Shop
statement: For each price, subtract the first subsequent price that is less than or equal to it, if one exists.
explanation: Use a monotonic stack of unresolved indices, or scan forward for the first qualifying discount.

title: Running Sum of 1d Array
statement: Return the running sum where output[i] is the sum of nums[0..i].
explanation: Maintain a cumulative total and append it for each element.
